assertion_analysis.fails_if: The fixture revision is not on main; a Git observation independent of the ledger input proves the merge precondition.
Either queued request did not enter awaiting-upstream.
Removing the obligations integration or shared derivation returns zero duties; duplicate emission also fails.
The emitted duty names another run or omits its run identity.
The emitted plan differs from the fixture plan; the expected input identity is independent of the output.
Section normalization emits s1, another section or no section instead of the public §1 identity.
The duty emits another revision or omits its head; expected revision was independently observed through git at line 98.
Waiter discovery omits, duplicates, reorders or misidentifies either held request.
The reported held count is not two.
The command omits or misidentifies the owning plan or section.
The action does not target the actual section declaration; execution is also checked at 185-188.
Session filtering leaks the upstream duty to an unrelated coordinator.
Session filtering assigns the duty to the waiting coordinator.
The positive setup for the done transition creates zero or multiple duties.
Removing the implementable-declaration guard leaves a duty after done.
Admission retains either waiter in awaiting-upstream after done; this asserts the exact requested phase transition, not eventual completion.
The positive setup for deferred produces zero or multiple duties.
The declaration guard treats deferred as implementable.
The positive setup for partial delivery produces zero or multiple duties.
Removing the run-specific partial-comment suppression leaves the duty present.
Recording partial delivery releases either held request.
Section-wide suppression incorrectly hides a later merged run, or an accounted run reappears.
The unmerged-control commit accidentally equals main, invalidating the control.
Removing the ancestry guard produces a duty for an unmerged commit; the other parametrization catches duties invented with no run.
The field projection refuses newly supported fields or produces a duty without a merged run.
An offered action is an expression that is not a call; malformed syntax also fails parsing before this assertion.
The real validated writer rejects either offered action.
Executing the offered partial action fails to suppress its run duty.
Executing the offered done action leaves a duty.
The done action clears duties for another reason without actually writing the done declaration.
Snapshot loses or alters a duty that the direct view retains; shared-helper empty output passes both sides, as recorded in the finding.
The fixture inadvertently creates a live upstream pointer, invalidating the pointer-removal control.
Departure filtering removes or alters an existing snapshot duty while the direct view retains it; common empty output remains a blind spot.

findings.text: non-blocking: Snapshot parity here and at line 208 compares two consumers of merged_section_items_by_session without independently asserting a nonempty duty for this fixture; returning no duty from their shared helper lets both assertions pass, so add an explicit count and expected run/waiter identities before checking parity (the separate positive test already guards universal duty loss).
